THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 28, 2019 - CITY HALL -
3:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
FEBRUARY 28, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Robin Kim, Artesia-Cerritos United
  Methodist Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Youth
  Basketball League Rookie III Division Team - Wildcats.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Proclamations were made as follows:

  African American Heritage Month Honorees:

  Alex H. Beanum (posthumously – First African American to serve as Mayor of
  the City of Cerritos. Trustee for the Southeast Mosquito Abatement District, 2nd
  Lieutenant U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Caltrans Transportation Engineer and
  Los Angeles County Commission on Disabilities Board Member).

  Emmett Hall Jr. (Cerritos Sheriff’s Station Volunteer on Patrol Lead Live Scan
  operator)

  Dr. Valencia Mayfield (30 year ABC Unified School District educator, Golden Bell
  Award recipient).

  John H. Moore (First African American to serve on the Cerritos Community
  College District Board of Trustees and to serve as President).

  Anna Titus (29 year ABC Unified School District educator and Cerritos Fine Arts
  and Historical Commission Chairperson).

  Lewie Woodson (1st Combat Engineer Battalion Adoption Committee Charter
  Member and former Cerritos Let Freedom Ring Committee Member).
 City of Cerritos  February 28, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 7

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Robert Buell spoke regarding parking restrictions and problems in the area of
  Dumont and 183rd.

  Daisy Legasca spoke regarding the Cerritos High School PTSA event,
  Alzheimer’s facility in Cerritos, Commission appointments and restaurants.

  Anna Titus commended Torrey Contreras, Director of Community
  Development, for his progressive and attentive response to her concerns.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted
  by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  February 14, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February 14, 2019
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 28,
  2019 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  2/28/2019  $1,889,031.74 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  February 28, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council Treasurer’s reports for the period ending January
  31, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending
  January 31, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Adoption of Ordinance
  Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of February 14, 2019:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1025, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING TITLE 9 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE BY
  ADDING CHAPTER 9.83, ESTABLISHING REGULATIONS FOR SIDEWALK VENDORS
  IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, AND AMENDING CHAPTER 9.48 OF THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE IN RESPONSE TO CALIFORNIA SENATE BILL 946 (2018),
  HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-2
  (COUNCIL).*
  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to waive full reading
  of and adopt Ordinance No. 1025, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  AMENDING TITLE 9 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING
  CHAPTER 9.83, ESTABLISHING REGULATIONS FOR SIDEWALK VENDORS IN
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS, AND AMENDING CHAPTER 9.48 OF THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE IN RESPONSE TO CALIFORNIA SENATE BILL 946 (2018),
  HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-2
  (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 5-0, to
  approve the following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING TITLE 22 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL
  CODE RELATING TO THE REGULATION, LOCATION, AND/OR OPERATION OF
  SELF-STORAGE FACILITIES IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN REFERENCED AS
  DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-1 (COUNCIL).*
 City of Cerritos  February 28, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 7

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Robert Buell expressed support for the proposed Ordinance.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Approve Development Code Amendment 2019-1, making the findings set forth
  in Cerritos Planning Commission Resolution No. 2019-1; and

  2. Waive full reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1026, AN ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING TITLE 22 OF THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE REGULATION, LOCATION, AND/OR
  OPERATION OF SELF-STORAGE FACILITIES IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS,
  HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-1
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1, Yokoyama “no”) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration of a proposal by the ABC Unified School District to
  construct an additional head start building at the Kennedy Elementary School
  property located at 17500 Belshire Avenue in Artesia (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.  A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Robert D. Crockett expressed his opposition to the proposal.

  Tu-Anh Long expressed her opposition to the proposal.

  Lew Gentiluomo expressed is opposition to the proposal.

  Tom Woodward, Supervisor of Child Development, ABC Unified School District,
  provided additional information regarding the proposal.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor
  closed the public hearing and public comments.
 City of Cerritos  February 28, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve
  the ABC Unified School District’s proposed project to construct an additional
  building at Kennedy Elementary School, and direct staff to communicate to
  ABC Unified School District leadership the suggestion to notify surrounding
  Cerritos residents and provide them the opportunity to comment prior to
  ABCUSD’s approval of proposed project plans (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:
  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of the terms of service for members of Cerritos
  Advisory Boards to align with the new even-numbered year election cycle
  resulting from the City’s compliance with the California Voter Rights
  Participation Act (Senate Bill 415) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to:
  1.  Direct staff to prepare the appropriate documents to change the two-year
  term of service for all Cerritos advisory boards to coincide with the new
  even-numbered year election cycle (generally May 1 of each even-
  numbered year through April 30 of each subsequent election year), ensure
  that all documents are consistent in terms of service and other
  administrative matters pertaining to advisory board service, and present
  them for the City Council’s review and consideration prior to December 31,
  2019; and
  2.  Direct staff to prepare the appropriate documents and initiate notice and
  advertising to solicit advisory board applications for a “gap” one-year term
  of service to generally span April 1, 2019 to April 30, 2020 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1359-19, a contract for
  construction of asphalt improvements in City of Cerritos parking lot, Project No.
  19441 (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  February 28, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1.  Award a contract in the amount of $457,485 for Construction of Asphalt
  Improvements in City of Cerritos Parking Lot, Project No. 19441, Bid No.
  1359-19, to Century Paving and reject all other bids; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:
  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Yokoyama, Mayor
  Pro Tem Solanki, and Mayor Pulido.

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session on February 28, 2019.

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney Services

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and supported by the majority of the City
  Council, to continue Closed Session Item 12A to the March 14, 2019 City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1, Yokoyama “no”) as follows:
  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  February 28, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 7

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:34 p.m.

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
